change.title: pr-38446-flat
change.description: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Federated recovery-codes model returned by getCredentials() has no id
findings.body: `getCredentials()` builds the recovery-codes model with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`. That method does not set an id. The stored `recoveryCodes` model does get an id at line 195, but it is dropped here. The OTP branch of the same method returns `myUser.getOtp()`, which now has an id. So the federated recovery credential has `getId() == null`. `CredentialDeleteHelper` (services/.../util/CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64) looks federated credentials up by id, so it can never match this one. `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` line 86-87 calls `removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId())`, which would get null. Call `model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId())` after creating it.

findings.title: Used-up cleanup still targets only the local store for federated credentials
findings.body: `getCredential` can now return a credential that lives in the user storage. The all-codes-used branch still calls `removeStoredCredentialById(id)`. `UserCredentialManager.removeStoredCredentialById` (model/storage/.../UserCredentialManager.java:114) delegates to the local credential store only, so it does nothing for a federated credential. The branch then adds the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action. That is probably acceptable, because the user storage's `updateCredential` replaces the old codes. But who consumes codes is now up to the storage provider. The test provider's `isValid` (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340) only checks that the code is in the list and never consumes it. As a result, `allCodesUsed()` is never true for federated credentials. Please state this contract, for example in the javadoc of `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, and make the test provider consume codes if the intent is to mirror `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid`.

findings.title: Optional introduced but immediately unwrapped with get()
findings.body: `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException` when no credential exists, exactly as the old `.findFirst().get()` did. Use `orElseThrow` with a clear message, or handle the empty case. Also note that for a federated credential `createFromValues` rebuilds the codes from the start. So `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` always returns number 1 for federated users, whatever the provider has consumed.

findings.title: Unneeded delayed-authenticator with typo'd alias; no negative case
findings.body: The delayed authenticator runs with delay 0 and adds nothing to the test. Its config alias `delayed-suthenticator-config` has a typo. It looks copy-pasted from RecoveryAuthnCodesAuthenticatorTest. `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` also only covers the success path. There is no check that a wrong code is rejected by the user storage. The test also does not check that the federated credential is shown or removable, which is where the missing id (see the finding on BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java line 237) would show up.

findings.title: Unrelated whitespace-only rewrites
findings.body:
The body of `getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory` is re-indented with no logic change. The same kind of noise appears in the test (`.auth(accountToken)` indentation, `TypeReference<>() {\n}`) and in the javadoc `

` in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage. Drop these hunks to keep the diff focused.

findings.title: Provider looked up before it is needed
findings.body: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")` runs even when the user storage handles the credential. It is only used in the else branch. Move the lookup into that branch. The hard-coded provider id mirrors the existing OTP helper ("keycloak-otp"), so that part is consistent.

contracts.action: Recovery codes are created through user storage first, then local DB (new CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, called from RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction)
contracts.equivalent_path: CredentialHelper.createOTPCredential (same file, lines 92-110), which tries user.credentialManager().updateCredential and falls back to the CredentialProvider.
contracts.before_after: Before, the action always called RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential. That deletes any existing local recovery credential and then creates a new one. Now the raw code list is serialized as JSON and passed to UserCredentialManager.updateCredential. For a federated user whose storage supports the type, the storage stores it. Otherwise the call returns false and the old local path runs unchanged. Local-user behaviour is identical.
contracts.visible_effect: For federated users on a storage that supports the type, codes are stored in the storage and login validates them there. Everyone else sees no change.
contracts.failure_mode: If the storage's updateCredential returns true, no local credential is created and no existing local credential is deleted. A stale local credential could then remain next to the federated one. getCredential prefers the federated one, but the validator order is not settled by this PR.

contracts.action: Recovery credential lookup: federated first, then local (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential), used by the login form bean and the form authenticator
contracts.equivalent_path: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid, which reads only getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream and consumes a code on success.
contracts.before_after: Before, the form bean and the authenticator read only local stored credentials. Now they read the federated credentials first. Validation itself (credentialManager().isValid) still goes through the storage validator and the local provider. Code consumption (removeRecoveryAuthnCode and updateStoredCredential) happens only in the local provider's isValid, so federated credentials get no consumption from Keycloak.
contracts.visible_effect: The enter-recovery-code form shows a code number taken from the federated credential, and the authenticator's all-codes-used handling runs against it.
contracts.failure_mode: For federated credentials the id is null in the test provider, and removeStoredCredentialById is local-only. Both are reported as findings above.

summary: The change routes recovery-code creation and lookup through user storage first and falls back to the local DB. It follows the existing OTP pattern, and the local path is unchanged. The issues are minor and mostly in the test provider and test. The federated recovery model from `getCredentials()` has a null id. The used-up cleanup in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` is local-only. The test provider never consumes codes, so the federated all-codes-used path is untested. The test has a copy-pasted delayed authenticator with a typo'd alias and no negative case. There are also unrelated whitespace edits. I did not find a blocker. I read the files only and did not build or run anything.
